Triage: → `domain:metadata`, queued. The divergence surfaces across the meta reads served by `packages/metadata-protocol`; the fold itself is `mergeObjectDefinitions` in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:137-140`. Re-laned from `domain:metadata-protocol` (not a lane-table label). Type intent: **Bug** (`type` field not set — `list_issue_types` 403 for this credential).

**PM ruling premise (mechanism-assumption grade — verify before coding, falsify loudly):** the existing code standard decides the "which side is right" question, so this is queued rather than escalated. `defineObjectExtension` accepts `label`, `mergeObjectDefinitions` documents scalar override as last-writer-wins, and the extension carries `priority: 210` — declared semantics say **the overlay label wins everywhere**, and the list/by-name reads are the under-reporting side. Re-check command: `git grep -n "last writer wins" packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` against `origin/main`. If you find an ADR or ruling that additive overlays must not rename their base object, **stop and report the fork — do not silently implement the other side.**

Deliverable includes the drift gate the filer names: extend both agreement pins past `fieldNamesOf` to the scalar triple (`label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`) across all three reads.

Serial constraints: same serving family as in-flight #8027, queued #8031 and #8038 (this round) — same-package serial, no two in one batch without confirmed file-surface disjointness.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, `opus`.

**Claim — `domain:metadata` PM seat (#6367).** PM session `session_01AmES43BMDg4bPrxTdi5q7t`, branch `claude/issue-8037-extension-label-leak`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`.

## ⚠️ This is the THIRD defect in the same family, and the pattern is now the point

#7556 (PR #8015) made the by-name `/meta` read fold `objectExtensions` contributors onto the MetadataService body — **reconciling the two reads on `fields`.** Since then:

| # | what the fold got wrong | found by |
|---|---|---|
| #8027 → PR **#8045** (landed `fa6dd59`) | `validations` and `indexes` **duplicated** — the fold is not idempotent, and two shipped call sites violated its documented precondition | the next card |
| **#8037 (this card)** | the extension's **`label`** leaks onto `?layers=true` only — the two reads now disagree on label | the next card |

⇒ **#8015's pin compared FIELD NAMES.** It was structurally blind to every other property of a merged object. I accepted that PR and called the pin excellent — it was, for the dimension it tested — and I did not ask what it did not cover. That gap has now produced two follow-on defects.

**Standing review criterion, recorded on #8045 and repeated here:** when a merge reconciles a *structure*, a pin over one of its keys proves nothing about the others. `mergeObjectDefinitions` treats `fields` (key-keyed spread, idempotent), `validations`/`indexes` (concatenated), and scalars like `label` (last-writer-wins) **three different ways** — so a fold has three distinct failure modes and a field-name pin sees none of them but its own.

## ⭐ What I want from this card beyond the label fix

⚠️ **Do not fix `label` and stop.** `mergeObjectDefinitions` has a small, enumerable set of merge behaviours. **Enumerate every property it touches, classify each by merge kind, and say for each whether the two reads agree.** If a fourth divergence exists, I would rather find it here than in a fourth card.

That enumeration is the deliverable I care most about; the `label` fix is the easy half.

## Region and concurrency

⚠️ The maintainer has raised concurrency to **8**, so `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` and `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` will have **several concurrent editors**. Every brief carries the same discipline: **declare your region, anchor on function names (never line numbers), merge `origin/main` before opening the PR, and merge again after each sibling lands.** A conflict is my cost, not yours — resolve it and say so.

⚠️ `protocol.ts` line numbers have gone stale **three times in one day**; this file has taken many merges today.

Brief carried **inline in the dev's prompt** — cloud containers still get **403 on every GitHub API call** (measured three times since the App was connected), so a brief that lives only here is unreadable to them.

**`Part of` closure — PR #8258 merged as `3a27c46edb`, and this card deliberately stays open.**

Re-graded `pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision` and unassigned, in one label write, because what remains is a maintainer call rather than dispatchable work.

## Delivered

The **property-class enumeration** (test-only, 708 insertions, no source change): `packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-property-classes.test.ts` plus a scalar-divergence dogfood test. It pins every property class `mergeObjectDefinitions` touches, so the next member of this family fails on a unit instead of arriving as a fourth card.

That was worth landing on its own. This family exists precisely because each pin was blind to the next defect: **#7556/#8015** reconciled `fields`; **#8027/#8045** then found `validations`/`indexes` duplicated — invisible to #8015's pin because that pin compares field *names* and the field spread is idempotent; **#8037** arrived next about `label`. Three different merge semantics — spread (idempotent), concatenation (not), last-writer-wins — and a pin over one proves nothing about the others.

## Remaining — and the premise correction

⚠️ **The `label` fix is NOT delivered, and the card's premise moved.** The dev's measurement **relocates the defect: the divergence is in i18n, not in the fold.** So this card was not satisfied; it was corrected.

⛔ **Blocking fork (maintainer's call, why this is `needs-user-decision`):**

> Should the catalog lose to an explicit override, or should the untranslated diagnostic be reconciled with the translated reads?

That is i18n precedence — product semantics, not an implementation detail. It was carried only in PR #8258's body until now; recording it here so the decision has its natural anchor. ⛔ Not dispatchable until ruled.

## Owner

`domain:metadata` seat (#6367). Returns to `pm:queue` the moment the fork is ruled.

## ⚠️ Related work that may absorb part of this

**#8268** was filed minutes ago from the #8038 dev's rescued handover: `GET /meta/object/:name` drops `nameField` for artifact-ingested objects. Its own caveat is directly relevant here — `nameField` is a **scalar property resolved last-writer-wins**, so it may already fall inside this card's enumeration. Whoever picks either up should read both first.

#8268 also argues the sharper framing: three materialization stamps have now diverged on one seam one at a time (#6562 injected system columns → #8038 `__search` → #8268 `nameField`), and the class is worth ruling on rather than the third instance. This card is the same lesson from the merge side.

**Dev report relayed by the PM** (its container is 403 on the whole GitHub API). ⚠️ **It corrects this card's premise, and it corrects my own review of PR #8258 — I under-read what was delivered.**

## ⚠️ First, a disclosure about the merge

PR #8258's body, as the dev wrote it, carried **"⛔ do not flip ready / no auto-merge"**. **I never saw that text.** The dev could not open the PR, so I opened #8258 myself from its pushed branch with a body I wrote, reviewed the diff, and merged it as `3a27c46edb`.

On the merits I still think the merge is right — test-only, no source change, `Part of` so it closes nothing, CI fully green, and the two `it.fails` cases are correct as shipped. But the instruction existed and I acted against it without knowing, so it goes on the record rather than being quietly absorbed. ⇒ **Lesson for this seat: when opening a PR on a 403-blocked dev's behalf, ask for its intended PR body *before* arming anything** — the body is where a dev puts its merge conditions, and reconstructing it loses them.

## ⭐ The headline: this is NOT a fold defect

`mergeObjectDefinitions` names exactly six keys and copies nothing else — confirmed from **both** sides (the function body, and `ObjectExtensionSchema`'s own guidance). **The fold has zero divergences across all six.** Measured, not argued:

```
[BYNAME] fold(showcase_account) baseLabel="Account" -> outLabel="Account (Success Overlay)"
[BYNAME] served label = "Account"          ← discarded downstream
[LAYERS] fold(...)                          -> outLabel="Account (Success Overlay)"
[LAYERS] served effective="Account (Success Overlay)"
```

The fold returns **the same body to both reads**. `translateObject` (`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`) then resolves each scalar as **`catalog ?? document`**; the showcase catalog declares `objects.showcase_account.label = "Account"`; list and by-name are translated, `?layers=true` is **deliberately** not. Hence "onto `?layers=true` only" — the symptom pointed at the one layer that is behaving.

⇒ **A fix applied to the fold would be applied to the only component that is correct.**

## ⛔ And the milder half was the one we were looking at

The same mechanism defeats **the tenant's own Studio rename** (`PUT`, 200 OK):

| Surface | Label |
|---|---|
| list / by-name | `Account` |
| `layers.overlay` | **`Customer`** ← what the tenant saved |
| `layers.effective` | `Account (Success Overlay)` |

The rename reaches **neither read a writable form derives from**. Filed as **#8284**, carrying the design ruling. That is a materially more severe defect than the extension-label leak this card was opened for.

## ⛔ Why the "easy half" was not shipped — and this is the part I most want on the record

I described the `label` fix as the deliverable and the enumeration as the supporting work. The dev reverse-verified per arm and **arm B — the card's proposed "fold drops scalars" — turns exactly ONE new case red (the anti-vacuity one) and is invisible to both existing pins** (#8015's agreement pin and #8045's fold pin stay green).

So the "easy half" would have: deleted a documented `ObjectExtensionSchema` feature, passed every pre-existing pin, made the symptom disappear, and left the tenant-rename defect untouched. **A regression that looks like a fix and that our existing tests could not see.** The dev shipped no behavioural change and asked for a ruling instead. That was the right call and it is the opposite of what my dispatch framing invited.

## What did land (`3a27c46edb`)

Test-only, no source files changed: the six-property enumeration across twelve host shapes, asserted **against the registry's resolved schema (ADR-0029 D9.2) — never against another route**, because *both* prior defects had the two routes agreeing with each other on a body that was already wrong. Plus the dogfood repro with two `it.fails` cases. Byte-identity preserved for objects with no contributor and no overlay (`toBe` reference-identity asserted); #8045's idempotency and the `layers.overlay` boundary untouched.

Gates: metadata-protocol 1094 ✅ · objectql 3390 ✅ · rest 1747 ✅ · runtime 2195 ✅ · dogfood 676 ✅ + 2 expected-fail (its own) · `check:type-check-debt` exit 0 on a built closure, **no ledger entry raised, no `--lower` on anyone's lines**.

## This card's status

Stays **`needs-user-decision`**, unassigned. The fork now lives properly on **#8284** with the full measurement and the arm-B evidence. This card remains the `label`-shaped entry point; ⛔ do not dispatch a fold-side fix against it.

⚠️ **`pluralLabel` and `description` carry the identical exposure** and are simply not triggered on `main` today (no shipped extension overrides `pluralLabel`; `showcase_account`'s catalog has no `description` key). Any ruling should cover all three scalars, not `label` alone.
